nodes.label: ARCHITECTURE.md — SIH 26122 System Architecture
nodes.rationale: Original point-in-time system specification converted from a PDF. Sections 0 and 5 carry the sharpest reasoning; sections 2 and parts of 7 are now historical because the shipped contracts drifted.

nodes.label: Retrieval and ranking are separate stages
nodes.rationale: Retrieval is recall-oriented (cast wide, top-20); ranking is precision-oriented feature scoring. Merging them into one opaque LLM call would destroy explainability and the audit trail.

nodes.label: Candidate Retrieval (tag exact, BM25, fuzzy, embedding)
nodes.rationale: Four recall-oriented channels run in parallel so that no single signal can lose a true candidate.

nodes.label: RRF Fusion
nodes.rationale: Reciprocal rank fusion merges the retrieval channels without requiring their scores to be comparable.

nodes.label: Feature Ranking
nodes.rationale: Deterministic weighted feature scoring, so the final score is a pure function of named features and can be swept in a grid search.

nodes.label: Confidence + Margin Decision (AUTO_LINK / REVIEW / NEW_ACTIVITY / REJECTED)
nodes.rationale: A low top-1 minus top-2 margin must force review even when the top score is high — 'confident but ambiguous' is the failure mode the margin guard exists to catch.

nodes.label: ScheduleActivity contract
nodes.rationale: One L5/L6 node from the parsed baseline, carrying wbs_path, discipline, tags, planned/actual dates, quantities and predecessors.

nodes.label: RawInput contract
nodes.rationale: One uploaded artifact or agent session. sha256 is required for deduplication — uploading the same artifact twice must not double-write progress. Never implemented as a model; its role is served by the Job row plus the uploaded file.

nodes.label: ExtractedEvent contract
nodes.rationale: One progress assertion before linking. Provenance (locator, char_span, raw_text) is non-negotiable — it is the spine of the audit trail.

nodes.label: LinkCandidate contract
nodes.rationale: One (event, activity) pair carrying its retrieval sources, rrf_score and the named feature vector that produced final_score.

nodes.label: LinkDecision contract
nodes.rationale: The adjudication, system or human, carrying confidence, margin, the thresholds in force and a deterministic rationale list.

nodes.label: AuditRecord contract (append-only)
nodes.rationale: Append-only record created for every field mutation. The audit log has no update path; corrections create a new record instead of mutating history.

nodes.label: DelayReason contract
nodes.rationale: The institutional-memory unit. The month field exists to enable seasonality and historical-delay queries.

nodes.label: Provenance (locator, char_span, raw_text)
nodes.rationale: A position shown is exact; no position shown means there is no single line to show, not that the line was lost. 165 of 259 audit rows carry an exact position.

nodes.label: date_basis provenance enum (EXPLICIT / RELATIVE_RESOLVED / DEFAULTED_TO_REPORT_DATE)
nodes.rationale: Specified so a planner can distinguish 'the line said 2 Aug' from 'the line said nothing so we used the report header date'. Deferred and never implemented; the write path still ignores it.

nodes.label: rationale is feature names, never LLM prose
nodes.rationale: Explanations must be deterministic and auditable; fluent model prose cannot be swept, compared, or defended in front of a planner.

nodes.label: Technology stack selection
nodes.rationale: Python 3.11 + Pydantic v2 + FastAPI + SQLite/SQLAlchemy + rank_bm25 + rapidfuzz + sentence-transformers + Ollama, chosen so one language covers extraction, matching and API with zero-setup persistence and an offline-capable inference path.

nodes.label: Offline preparation posture
nodes.rationale: Wheelhouse download, committed lockfile, locally cached node_modules and pre-pulled Ollama models, because venue internet must be assumed unavailable.

nodes.label: 'On submission' rather than 'near real time'
nodes.rationale: 'Near real time' implies streaming, WebSockets and background workers. Nothing here needs it — ingest is a synchronous POST returning in under 3 seconds on 120 activities.

nodes.label: Institutional memory promoted to a primary outcome
nodes.rationale: Every team will build ingest→extract→link; institutional memory is the only defensible differentiator and is cheap because it is SQL over data already captured. Real but thin: 47 of 120 activities have both an actual start and finish.

nodes.label: Ranked cut list
nodes.rationale: Eight items ranked first-to-remove, starting with XER parsing and PMXML export write-back, so time pressure is spent against a pre-agreed order instead of improvised.

nodes.label: Never-cut core (reconciliation, review queue, eval.py, provenance spans, one memory query)
nodes.rationale: These five elements are the core pitch; everything else is packaging.

nodes.label: Risk A — the tag may be doing all the matching work
nodes.rationale: Line and equipment tags are near-decisive evidence. Cheapest test: run eval.py twice, once with tags stripped from event text; if precision collapses, the dataset is too tag-dependent.

nodes.label: Risk B — generated ground truth is circular
nodes.rationale: If one model generates both the DPR text and its label, evaluation measures agreement with the generator's intent. Cheapest test: two teammates independently relabel 40 sampled mentions and report inter-annotator agreement. Never run.

nodes.label: Risk C — local inference may fail at the venue
nodes.rationale: Cold model startup, CPU throttling and RAM pressure. Cheapest test is airplane mode on a fresh boot of the actual demo laptop; if a 7B pass exceeds ~20s per DPR, move extraction toward rules.

nodes.label: link_confidence on GET /schedule is derived per request
nodes.rationale: Not stored; read back off the audit trail as one grouped query so the Schedule table can show per-row confidence without 120 audit requests. Safe only because the audit table is append-only.

nodes.label: The time agent fills slots by regex, not by an LLM
nodes.rationale: POST /agent/turn is conversational and stateful, but slot extraction is regex and keyword matching. Stated plainly because the conversation is convincing enough to be mistaken for a model.

nodes.label: Source-conflict detection was scoped to one upload
nodes.rationale: Real disagreements are across uploads, so a per-request accumulator found nothing; 24 genuine disagreements existed while integrity_warnings reported zero. Fixed by reading the prior audit write before each date write.

nodes.label: Source files were decoded lossily and the damage was permanent
nodes.rationale: DPRs are cp1252; errors='replace' wrote U+FFFD into raw_text, source_span and the audit trail. Re-ingesting could not fix it. Decode chain is now utf-8-sig, cp1252, latin-1 — cp1252 before latin-1 because latin-1 accepts any byte and would mask the others.

nodes.label: Resetting has to survive a schema change
nodes.rationale: SQLAlchemy create_all adds missing tables but never missing columns, so a stale database failed mid-demo on first insert. reset_demo now compares model columns against the live database and rebuilds when they differ.

nodes.label: DECISIONS.md — architectural history
nodes.rationale: The source code says what changed; this file says why. Superseded decisions are never deleted, only marked and linked.

nodes.label: D-001 — Retrieval and ranking are separate stages
nodes.rationale: Explainability and a preserved audit trail. Must be read together with H-003, the single-LLM-call design it replaced.

nodes.label: D-002 — Precision-first decision rule with a margin guard
nodes.rationale: A wrong auto-link corrupts a schedule, so coverage is traded for precision and top-1/top-2 separation must exceed margin_min. Qualified by H-014: the running server does not use the operating point the headline metric comes from.

nodes.label: D-003 — rationale is deterministic feature names, never LLM prose
nodes.rationale: Explanations must be auditable and comparable across runs.

nodes.label: D-004 — The audit trail is append-only
nodes.rationale: Corrections write a new row; history is never mutated. This is what makes derived projections such as link_confidence safe.

nodes.label: D-005 — The LLM is optional and off by default
nodes.rationale: EXTRACTION_PROVIDER defaults to rules. An Ollama outage must never be a NAVIS outage; every failure mode falls back silently and keeps collected slots.

nodes.label: D-006 — Tags are never taken from the LLM
nodes.rationale: tag_overlap is the highest-weighted feature and acts as a floor via line_locked; a hallucinated tag corrupts linking with near-decisive force. Tags come only from the regex pre-pass, even when it finds none.

nodes.label: D-007 — Unitless quantities cannot drive percent-complete
nodes.rationale: 'All 12 pockets grouted' against a node planned as 48 m3 would silently register 25% complete. A unitless quantity is excluded and a note recorded.

nodes.label: D-008 — actual_finish is written only at 100% complete
nodes.rationale: Partial-scope protection: a DPR line covering part of a node's scope must not finish the whole node. A finish asserted below 100% is recorded as a conflict, not applied.

nodes.label: D-009 — Agent/voice updates are proposals, never direct writes
nodes.rationale: Supersedes D-009a, where the agent wrote actual dates directly with auto_applied=True and created no review item, so a voice update bypassed the planner entirely. POST /review/{id}/resolve is now the only path that commits an actual date.

nodes.label: D-010 — Source files are decoded explicitly, never lossily
nodes.rationale: A lossy decode is permanent and propagates into the audit trail. extraction/textio.py owns the decode chain.

nodes.label: D-011 — Source conflicts are detected across uploads via the audit trail
nodes.rationale: Supersedes D-011a (per-request accumulator scope). Nothing new is stored — the conflict list is derived by walking each activity's writes per field in the append-only audit trail.

nodes.label: D-012 — SQLite, synchronous ingest, and 'on submission'
nodes.rationale: At ~120 activities Postgres and async machinery buy failure modes rather than throughput. Read together with H-007.

nodes.label: D-013 — Adopt a persistent repository memory protocol
nodes.rationale: Conversational memory does not survive a context reset, a new machine, a new developer or a different agent — and the project's most important properties look like removable complexity to someone who does not know why they exist. Establishes CLAUDE.md, DECISIONS.md and FLOW.md as permanent root files.

nodes.label: D-014 — Backfill history as a parallel H-series; document defects rather than fix them
nodes.rationale: Renumbering would break every cross-reference and falsely imply the entries were written at the time. Fixing and documenting in one pass would make both untrustworthy — a defect fixed in the commit that first describes it leaves no record it was ever live.

nodes.label: H-001 — Re-scoped from 'WhatsApp photo → Gantt' to PS 26122
nodes.rationale: The project began against a paraphrase of the problem statement, not its text. Rebuilt against the PS: the words WhatsApp, photo and Gantt appear nowhere in the shipped system.

nodes.label: H-002 — The no-code stack (Lovable + Supabase) was abandoned for Python
nodes.rationale: Three constraints point the same way: offline operation, auditability (a generated app cannot produce a FeatureVector or an append-only audit trail), and measurement (eval.py needs decide_outcome to be a pure function). The 'zero manual coding' constraint is no longer true and must not be claimed.

nodes.label: H-003 — V1 matching (one LLM call picks the task) was abandoned before it shipped
nodes.rationale: Three concrete failures: a model-emitted match_confidence cannot be calibrated or swept; there is no top-1 vs top-2 margin so 'confident but ambiguous' is undetectable; and the explanation is prose. Residue still in the code: schedule_context, alternatives, reasoning, match_method values.

nodes.label: H-004 — The CPM / dependency-recalculation engine was never built
nodes.rationale: Dropped at the architecture stage, not lost at implementation. Standard PM libraries already push dependent tasks; the value-add is automated ingestion of informal updates, not reinventing scheduling logic. predecessors survives only as a matching feature.

nodes.label: H-005 — Photo evidence and the vision path were never built
nodes.rationale: Verifying a photo shows a completed task is a hard vision problem, and the PS explicitly waives production OCR. Vision would buy a capability the PS does not ask for at the cost of the ingestion quality it does.

nodes.label: H-006 — Institutional memory promoted from secondary to primary
nodes.rationale: Four memory queries computed from captured execution data, with the sample size shown next to every figure. Suggestions are suppressed below two completions.

nodes.label: H-007 — 'Near real time' downgraded to 'on submission'
nodes.rationale: Measured 266 events in 1.86s, ~7ms/event. The budget was never the problem, so async machinery would have bought failure modes and a polling UI for nothing. The Job table is the vestige, still useful as an ingestion record.

nodes.label: H-008 — Export was built and import was not, the reverse of the plan
nodes.rationale: PMXML and XER export shipped; PMXML import never did, and /ingest rejects .xml and .xer. Most likely because export is self-contained while import needed a real PMXML sample the team did not have.

nodes.label: H-009 — Contract-first Pydantic models, and how the contracts drifted
nodes.rationale: The method held — extraction/ knows nothing about matching/, matching/ reads nothing from the database — but many specified fields never shipped, so ARCHITECTURE.md §2 is now a historical specification.

nodes.label: H-010 — Embeddings: bge-small-en-v1.5 (spec) → all-MiniLM-L6-v2 with hashed fallback
nodes.rationale: Both are 384-dimensional so the swap is drop-in; MiniLM is smaller and most likely already cached. The deterministic hashed-trigram fallback means import matching never fails — but it is silent, so eval.py's embedder line is the only routine check.

nodes.label: H-011 — LLM: qwen2.5:7b-instruct (spec) → qwen3:8b with grammar-constrained decoding
nodes.rationale: format is given the full JSON Schema, not the string 'json', so Ollama compiles it to a grammar and enum fields cannot go out of vocabulary. think:false is sent explicitly because a think block breaks structured output. is_available() also checks the model is actually pulled.

nodes.label: H-012 — pandas and lxml were designed in and never used
nodes.rationale: A DataFrame loses the sheet position, and the audit trail needs source_row on every event. The hand-written openpyxl parser keeps it. lxml went with H-008: there is no import path to parse.

nodes.label: H-013 — One seeded generator builds the whole corpus, and the circularity is admitted
nodes.rationale: generate_all.py with a fixed seed emits the baseline, 10 DPRs, two spreadsheets and 254 labelled mentions. The mention list is written next to the prose so label and text cannot drift. Weakest measured number: NO_MATCH rejection at 8.3% on only 12 hard negatives.

nodes.label: H-014 — Four threshold sets exist and the demo does not run the headline one
nodes.rationale: They are calibrated on different input distributions: eval.py scores gold mentions (0.775 → 100% precision at 50.4% coverage) while the live server runs 0.70 on real extraction spans (96.6% precision at 48%). No claim of 100% should be made about the running demo without naming the threshold set.

nodes.label: H-015 — The first real bug: dates were extracted and then dropped
nodes.rationale: Dates were resolved into hints and never bound to the event, so every date-dependent consumer treated None as 'signal absent' by design and failed silently. The same failure mode is still available because every FeatureVector field is Optional.

nodes.label: H-016 — date_basis provenance was specified and deliberately deferred
nodes.rationale: A planner cannot distinguish an asserted date from a defaulted one. Reinstating it is one enum, one field and one column, and is the cheapest available improvement to audit legibility.

nodes.label: H-017 — Start and finish became distinct assertions; the forecast guard was added
nodes.rationale: is_forecast_language() lives in code rather than the prompt so it holds for every provider and cannot be talked out of by a model. DateAssertion keeps each claim individually rather than collapsing to min/max so a disagreement stays visible.

nodes.label: H-018 — The Ollama path was added opt-in, with guards against three named model errors
nodes.rationale: The blast radius of each error is asymmetric — a missed tag costs recall on one event; a hallucinated tag corrupts a link. Every guard is written on the side of the smaller blast radius, and the guards shipped with the feature rather than after an incident.

nodes.label: H-019 — Schedule context removed from the LLM prompt; a messy DPR added
nodes.rationale: Re-sending ~3,000 tokens of schedule per span cost more than the inference itself — the first call of every run stalled past its timeout on prefill — to produce a field no consumer reads. dpr_day_11_messy.txt was added in the same commit and is deliberately outside ground truth.

nodes.label: H-020 — Reproducibility pass; 12k lines of export artifacts left Git
nodes.rationale: An airplane-mode cold run is impossible without pinned dependencies and a one-command seed. requirements.txt is annotated with why each package is there, including python-multipart which no grep for imports would find.

nodes.label: H-021 — CORS: the frontend became a second process
nodes.rationale: Vite hot reload was worth more than a single deployable artefact. Consequence: two processes must run, and the broad allowed-origin list is a demo posture, not a security posture.

nodes.label: H-022 — Design-first UI: 22 mockups produced before the screens
H-023 — Two roles, and a clarification loop back to the supervisor
nodes.rationale: Field Supervisor and Planning Engineer, with POST /review/{id}/clarify closing the loop back to the person who filed the update.

nodes.label: H-024 — The field app has no offline capture, and is built never to claim one
nodes.rationale: No service worker, no IndexedDB. Field.tsx deliberately never claims a save succeeded, in line with the honesty policy.

nodes.label: H-025 — Three commits named 'Update SIH project'
nodes.rationale: Historical note recording what is actually inside three uninformatively-named commits.

nodes.label: H-026 — The 'cline checkpoint' commits are tooling residue
nodes.rationale: Tooling artefacts, not project history; recorded so a future reader does not mine them for intent.

nodes.label: H-027 — Publishing the number that undercuts the architecture
nodes.rationale: The ablation showing the shipped hybrid ranks worse than plain BM25 was published in the repository rather than suppressed.

nodes.label: FLOW.md — how execution travels through NAVIS
nodes.rationale: Real file, function and class names only; never invented architecture. Carries a per-task Current Modification Area.

nodes.label: Execution flow evolution V0 → V1 → V1a → V2
nodes.rationale: V0 planned and never built; V1 specified and immediately corrected; V1a the agent writing directly to the schedule, superseded by D-009; V2 current.

nodes.label: Primary path — document ingestion (POST /ingest)
nodes.rationale: extract → match → roll up → persist → return, synchronously in one request.

nodes.label: Planner reconciliation path — the only route that commits an actual date
nodes.rationale: POST /review/{id}/resolve is the single authorised write path for actual_start and actual_finish.

nodes.label: Conversational agent path (POST /agent/turn)
nodes.rationale: A second ingestion surface producing the same ExtractedEvent contract via agent_slots.py and _create_event_from_slots.

nodes.label: Module relationships and contracts (extraction / matching / server / frontend)
nodes.rationale: matching/ reads nothing from the database — it is pure over the baseline JSON — which is exactly why the alias lexicon cannot be consulted at retrieval time.

nodes.label: Threshold configuration map
nodes.rationale: The single most confusing thing in the codebase: four non-interchangeable threshold sets. Rules for quoting a number are stated here.

nodes.label: Technical debt, dead code and live defects register
nodes.rationale: Ten entries including two live bugs (resolve action names, .csv accepted but unparseable), the unreachable _dense_cos duplicate, the unreachable REJECTED branch, and the 0/0 nos → 100% case that is real but not the bug it looks like.

nodes.label: Documentation status — which files are current and which are dated
nodes.rationale: A documented contradiction is safer than a silently corrected one: ARCHITECTURE.md §2 and parts of §7, plus both build plans, are named as historical.

nodes.label: Current Modification Area
nodes.rationale: Required to be accurate for the work just completed at the end of every repository-changing task.

nodes.label: CLAUDE.md — Repository Operating Rules
nodes.rationale: Governs how any AI agent must work in this repository; permanent across sessions, machines, developers and agents.

nodes.label: The Prime Rule — read and maintain DECISIONS.md and FLOW.md
nodes.rationale: A repository-changing task is not complete until those files represent the resulting architecture, and the work is committed and pushed so the remote stays synchronized.

nodes.label: Source-of-truth model (CODE / FLOW / DECISIONS / CLAUDE / GIT)
nodes.rationale: Documentation that contradicts the code is worse than no documentation, because it is trusted.

nodes.label: Mandatory workflow (read → implement → verify → document → commit → push)
nodes.rationale: Verification comes before commit; broken code is never committed to satisfy the rules.

nodes.label: Verification commands (pytest 264, vitest 55, tsc, eval.py, healthcheck)
nodes.rationale: Any change to matching/, extraction/ or the thresholds must be followed by python eval.py, and a change that moves auto-link precision off 100% is a correctness regression, not a tuning result.

nodes.label: Project-specific constraints table
nodes.rationale: Eight standing constraints, each mapped to the DECISIONS.md entry that justifies it, so no agent reverses one without reading why it exists.

nodes.label: Git rules and secrets policy
nodes.rationale: Never force-push; never commit .env, credentials, dataset/uploads/, *.db or *.7z; a task can complete its code changes while Git synchronization fails, and that distinction must never be hidden.

nodes.label: Audit-1.md — independent gap analysis against PS 26122
nodes.rationale: Every number re-derived by executing the code (264 pytest, 55 vitest, eval.py, direct sqlite3 queries) rather than read from the repository's own documentation. 11 findings, 5 not previously documented.

nodes.label: F-01 — The matching engine ranks worse than plain BM25, and the defense is buried
nodes.rationale: BM25 alone is 93.8% top-1 against the shipped hybrid's 87.2%, and 37x faster. The real answer is in bm25gate.json: BM25 ranks better but gates worse — 35.0% vs 50.4% coverage at 100% auto-precision. The product is the calibrated decision, not the ranking.

nodes.label: F-02 — At 50.4% coverage, half the manual reconciliation still happens
F-03 — The learning loop is open: the system cannot get better
nodes.rationale: alias_lexicon rows are written on planner resolution and never read, because matching/ has no database dependency at all.

nodes.label: F-04 — Institutional memory, the stated differentiator, is statistically empty
nodes.rationale: The mechanism is real; the contents are near-empty on the seeded corpus.

nodes.label: F-05 — Planners can never teach the system a new delay cause
nodes.rationale: _compute_delay_reasons' second loop iterates reasons.keys(), so a planner's resolution note can only reinforce a cause the audit pass already found and can never introduce a new one.

nodes.label: F-06 — Inferred finish dates create zero-day durations that poison the memory store
nodes.rationale: Five zero-day durations out of 47 completed activities, produced by the max(reported_date) fallback in RollupAccumulator.results().

nodes.label: F-07 — One-to-many linking is absent, and the ground truth cannot reveal it
nodes.rationale: Many-to-one roll-up is strong; one mention spanning several nodes cannot be represented, and the label format hides the gap.

nodes.label: F-08 — The field app cannot capture anything without connectivity
F-09 — A dead duplicate of the exact method that needs fixing
nodes.rationale: The unreachable _dense_cos / _unique_line duplicate — the danger is editing the dead copy and measuring no change.

nodes.label: F-10 — No schedule import: the PS names Primavera/MS Project exports as an input
nodes.rationale: /ingest rejects .xml and .xer; PMXML and XER exist as export only.

nodes.label: F-11 — No authentication, no multi-project isolation
nodes.rationale: Single SQLite file, no project_id, broad CORS. A demo posture, not a security posture.

nodes.label: Verified metrics table (re-run 2026-08-30)
nodes.rationale: 100% auto-link precision, 50.4% coverage, 87.2% top-1 (70.1% tags stripped), 8.3% NO_MATCH rejection, ~7ms/event, 319 tests passing.

nodes.label: Audit-1 ranked order of work
nodes.rationale: Sequenced by leverage, not severity: dead code + densefix first because it is free measured accuracy; the learning loop third because it has the highest narrative payoff per hour.

nodes.label: FINDINGS.md — second independent review from the pushed branch
nodes.rationale: Cloned the pushed branch and compared code against the PS text; where docs and code disagree, the code is quoted.

nodes.label: F1 — Eleven activities share one finish date; two have zero duration
nodes.rationale: matching/engine.py:330 falls back to max(report dates) when no finish is asserted, and dpr_day_10.txt is dated 15/09/2026, so every completion in the last DPR is stamped with the day the report was written. It contradicts the project's best claim — that a wrong date is never written.

nodes.label: F2 — '50.4% coverage' counts mentions; the schedule received eleven rows
nodes.rationale: The real funnel is 254 mentions → 128 auto-linked → 76 nodes touched → 11 nodes dated. The last drop is the quantity guard, which is precisely why precision is 100% — present the funnel rather than the point metric.

nodes.label: F3 — The PS names Primavera exports as an input; NAVIS only writes them
nodes.rationale: A minimal PMXML reader changes the answer from 'we wrote the baseline' to 'we parsed it, and here is the file'.

nodes.label: F4 — The learning loop is write-only
nodes.rationale: AliasLexicon rows are written at server/main.py:1301 and nothing in matching/ imports it, while main.py's docstring claims corrections are persisted as a training signal. Wiring it into retrieval buys a closed-loop demo beat.

nodes.label: F5 — New scope and uncertain matches are indistinguishable
nodes.rationale: Nothing is dropped, but genuinely new scope arrives in the queue looking identical to a match the system merely was not sure about. Do not retune thresholds before the deadline — say it plainly instead.

nodes.label: F6 — Thirty-one review rows carry a wrong top suggestion
nodes.rationale: Precision-first protects the schedule, not the planner's attention. The fix is rehearsal: deliberately reject a wrong suggestion on stage.

nodes.label: F7 — An activity with zero planned quantity reports 100% complete
nodes.rationale: PIP-PCD-1053 reads 0/0 nos at 100.0%. Small alone, but it sits beside the F1 dates in the table a judge reads.

nodes.label: PS requirement coverage table (FINDINGS)
nodes.rationale: Twelve PS outcomes graded Built / Partial / Missing / Correctly cut, each with file-level evidence.

nodes.label: SIH-2026-PS.txt — Problem Statement 26122
nodes.rationale: Intelligent Data Capture & Schedule-Linking Layer for Infrastructure Project Management — the authoritative requirement the shipped system answers.

nodes.label: PS outcome — ingest heterogeneous discipline-wise inputs
nodes.rationale: Free-text daily reports, spreadsheets, scanned diaries and Primavera/MS Project exports, extracting activity-level actual start/end events.

nodes.label: PS outcome — LLM-based conversational or voice 'time agent'
nodes.rationale: Replaces rigid manual forms for site supervisors while still producing structured output.

nodes.label: PS outcome — fuzzy-match and link to the correct L5/L6 plan node
nodes.rationale: Must handle terminology differences and granularity mismatches, and flag unmatched or new activities for planner review rather than silently dropping them.

nodes.label: PS outcome — auto-update actuals with a confidence score and audit trail
nodes.rationale: Stated as 'in near real time', per entry.

nodes.label: PS outcome — institutional memory as a co-equal outcome
nodes.rationale: A growing queryable repository of real execution patterns — actual durations, recurring delay causes, discipline-wise productivity — so knowledge does not stay locked in supervisors' experience.

nodes.label: PS constraint — full production-grade OCR/ASR is not required
nodes.rationale: A prototype ingesting 2-3 varied input formats is stated to be ideal, and live project data will not be shared — teams work with synthetic data of similar structure.

nodes.label: SIH context.txt — original project context (2026-08-22)
nodes.rationale: Superseded framing. Kept for its competitive analysis, risk list and honesty policy, not as a description of the shipped system.

nodes.label: The 'WhatsApp photo → Gantt' paraphrase
nodes.rationale: The problem as originally understood: capture site photos or WhatsApp text updates, map them to a task, mark it progressed and recalculate the Gantt.

nodes.label: Zero manual coding constraint
nodes.rationale: Solutions had to be achievable via AI app builders or no-code platforms. This constraint was later abandoned and must no longer be claimed of the repository.

nodes.label: Mandatory human-confirmation gate before a status change
nodes.rationale: A wrongly-marked complete task triggers crew dispatch and material orders, and in an oil-field context premature progression to the next phase. One of only two ideas from the early framing that survived intact.

nodes.label: Dependency recalculation is not something to build from scratch
nodes.rationale: Standard PM libraries already handle 'if task X slips, push dependents'; the value-add is automated ingestion of informal updates into such an engine.

nodes.label: Honesty policy — flag what is simulated rather than idealised
nodes.rationale: If a judge finds a string in the product claiming autonomous verification, the honesty of the whole pitch is in question. Still visible in the sample-size labels and in ARCHITECTURE.md §7.

nodes.label: Competitive landscape (OpenSpace, Buildots, ALICE, Track3D, Xpedeon)
nodes.rationale: Existing tools are built around dedicated 360-degree camera rigs; the differentiation angle is informal low-friction input plus fit to Indian PSU/EPC conditions.

nodes.label: SIH26122 7-Day Build Plan (v1)
nodes.rationale: Superseded specification written against the paraphrase, not the PS text.

nodes.label: SIH26122 7-Day Build Plan (v2)
nodes.rationale: Revision with a corrected role map and a fixed tool stack 'decided up front — do not re-litigate mid-week'. Stale as an engineering document.

nodes.label: SIH26122 7-Day Build Plan v2 (PDF)
nodes.rationale: PDF rendering of the v2 build plan. Content not machine-read in this pass (no PDF renderer available); identity inferred from the filename and from DECISIONS.md H-002.

nodes.label: SIH26122 Team Build Guide (PDF)
nodes.rationale: Per DECISIONS.md H-002, the Team Build Guide PDFs describe the abandoned no-code stack and the team's role assignments, and are stale as engineering documents. Content not machine-read in this pass.

nodes.label: SIH26122 Team Build Guide rev2 (PDF)
nodes.rationale: Revision 2 of the Team Build Guide. Content not machine-read in this pass.

nodes.label: The no-code stack (Lovable.dev + Supabase + Claude API Edge Function)
nodes.rationale: Fixed up front under the rule that every line of code is AI-generated and humans only read, test and direct. Abandoned: no offline path, no place to hold a precision-first gate, and nowhere to put a test suite.

nodes.label: parse-update — one LLM call picks the task (V1 matching)
nodes.rationale: A Supabase Edge Function that injects a compact rendering of the whole schedule into the prompt and returns matched_task_id, match_confidence, alternatives and free-text reasoning. Acceptance bar was 80% top-1 on 60-80 messages.

nodes.label: Day 3 — dependency recalculation and a live Gantt
nodes.rationale: Topological sort, cycle detection, earliest_start = max(predecessor finishes) + lag, projected stored separately from planned. Named the highest single-point-of-failure in the plan's own risk register; never built.

nodes.label: Day 4 — photo evidence and the human gate
nodes.rationale: A vision call constrained to describe, not conclude, with the caption shown beside the photo as human-reviewable evidence. Never built; the human gate survived without it.

nodes.label: ROADMAP.md — Senior PM review, decoded and architected
nodes.rationale: Design document, no code changed. Uses [SAID] for what the PM stated and [INFERRED] for additions from industry practice, so an assumption is never mistaken for advice.

nodes.label: Latest Update 1-09-26.md
nodes.rationale: Byte-identical duplicate of ROADMAP.md.

nodes.label: The two-destination model
nodes.rationale: The spine everything else hangs off: field input becomes immutable evidence, then a proposal, then either the project layer or the knowledge layer — never both by the same route.

nodes.label: Evidence layer (immutable)
nodes.rationale: Written on arrival, always, unconditionally, never edited or deleted. It is the audit spine.

nodes.label: Proposal layer
nodes.rationale: A proposal is not a fact. It carries confidence and provenance and can be rejected without losing the evidence.

nodes.label: Project layer (official plan)
nodes.rationale: Written only by an authorised path — auto-link above threshold or PM approval — and every write emits an AuditRecord. Planned/baseline dates are immutable; only actuals are ever written.

nodes.label: Knowledge layer (lessons, norms, cross-project)
nodes.rationale: Written only from approved project data, never from raw proposals — a lesson learned from an unverified claim is worse than no lesson.

nodes.label: Physical-progress EVM (PV, EV, SV, SPI in work units)
nodes.rationale: Value measured in weighted work units rather than rupees, duration-weighted because every activity has dates but not every one has a quantity. AC/ACWP cannot be computed and must not be faked.

nodes.label: RAID (Risks, Actions, Issues, Decisions)
nodes.rationale: Delay reasons, the review queue and the audit trail already exist as raw material; the register is not assembled.

nodes.label: Semantic layer (domain model + controlled vocabulary + mapping layer)
nodes.rationale: Should not be an OWL ontology or a graph database yet — at 120 activities those add months and buy nothing demonstrable. Three quarters already exists: DISCIPLINE_META, alias_lexicon, tag normalisation, wbs_path, Pydantic contracts.

nodes.label: Canonical activity-type vocabulary
nodes.rationale: The important missing piece: a lesson must key on what kind of work this was (e.g. SPOOL_ERECTION_LARGE_BORE) so it transfers to a project with different activity IDs. Without it knowledge handoff cannot cross projects.

nodes.label: Knowledge handoff module
nodes.rationale: Stores lessons per activity type with conditions and context so future projects retrieve them; a separate module by design.

nodes.label: Three roles (Field Supervisor, Project Manager, Senior Management)
nodes.rationale: NAVIS ships two; Senior Management is the missing third, and information classification decides what each sees.

nodes.label: The verification workflow and its twelve-element evidence panel
nodes.rationale: The PM must see original input, what the AI understood, findings, source and proposed update, in that order — that ordering is what makes it trustworthy.

nodes.label: Extended evaluation module (RMSE, R2, calibration, per-class breakdown)
nodes.rationale: Maps the six requested metrics onto tasks and names where they are insufficient.

nodes.label: MVP triage — MUST / SHOULD / POST-MVP
nodes.rationale: What the PM described is a 6-12 month project-controls platform with at least nine missing subsystems; the honest answer before a deadline is four things, none longer than a day.

nodes.label: DEMO.md — demo runbook
nodes.rationale: Every step has been run end to end against a live server; the numbers shown are what it actually produced.

nodes.label: Known-good state after a reset
nodes.rationale: 120 activities, 13 files, 266 events, 148 auto-linked, 118 pending review, 67 with actual dates, 47 completed, 274 audit records, 75 source conflicts. A mismatch means the dataset is wrong, not the run.

nodes.label: The ASR transcript review step is the point, not an obstacle
nodes.rationale: Speech recognition mangles tags like 24"-P-1001-A1A, and tag overlap is the matcher's strongest feature, so the supervisor edits the transcript before it is sent.

nodes.label: The audit drawer as the forensic view
nodes.rationale: Every write newest-first with field, old → new value, source file and exact line or spreadsheet row, confidence at the time, and whether it was automatic or planner-confirmed. Where a row shows a file but no line, the drawer says 'no single line' rather than inventing one.

nodes.label: SETUP.md — environment setup from nothing (Windows)
The embedding model must be cached before any offline demo
nodes.rationale: Without a cached sentence-transformer the system silently degrades to the hashed-ngram embedder, producing materially worse dense recall with nothing in the API saying so.

nodes.label: The LLM is optional and OFF by default (setup)
nodes.rationale: Setup instructions state plainly that no Ollama installation is needed for a full run.

nodes.label: AGENTS.md — code-review-graph MCP tool protocol
nodes.rationale: Narrow scope with the knowledge graph first, then read the source. When the graph and the source disagree, the source wins; an empty result can mean 'not indexed', not 'does not exist'.
